newsitem.title: UK: Manchester United up on pay-per-view hopes.
newsitem.headline: Manchester United up on pay-per-view hopes.

text.p: Shares in Manchester United Plc bounced back from recent weakness on Thursday after a report in the Independent said pay-per-view broadcasts of live games in the UK premier soccer league could start as early as next year.
Manchester United shares, which have retreated from their record 594p set on October 14, were up 9p at 515 by 1043 GMT.

The Independent said executives from satellite broadcaster BSkyB were in informal talks with several top soccer clubs which could see Saturday matches transmitted at 10 stg a time, generating total revenues of up to 2.5 billion stg.
Sky plans to launch a digital satellite service next year, offering up to 200 new channels with at least 60 reserved for pay-per-view, the Independent said.
Among other quoted soccer clubs Tottenham Hotspur Plc was up 1p at 531-1/2, though no trades were recorded in the stock, while Chelsea Village was unchanged at 119-1/2p.
